FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Violence against women and children is one form of act that violates human rights, because the right to protection from violence of a woman that has been guaranteed by the 1945 Constitution and the Law on Human Rights has been violated by the perpetrator of violence, which should be respected and enforced to enhance human dignity, welfare and justice for such women. The impact of such violence causes women or children to suffer physically, psychologically, mentally, sexually, so they need to receive protection and health rehabilitation services, social rehabilitation, repatriation and legal assistance carried out in an integrated manner by victim service providers established by the Government, Regional Government and the community.

The protection and empowerment of women and children is currently a focus in development. Women and children are usually made into one unit in the scope of their regulation so that it is not focused and results in ambiguity between women and children. Women can be adults or children, while children can be female or male. In the division of authority as determined in Law Number 23 Year 2014 concerning Regional Government, it has been focused on the scope of each form of handling, namely women and children are not a unity. In that context, regionally related to women and children, regional regulations must be present concerning: a). Fulfillment of Children's Rights and Special Protection of Children, b). Gender Mainstreaming, c). Protection of Witnesses/Victims and Prevention of Trafficking in Persons, and d). Protection and Empowerment of Women and Children From Acts of Violence. These four regional regulations are a package that must be regulated by the Regional Government in accordance with its authority.

c. social rehabilitation;

CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1 In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is the Region of Balangan Regency.
2. Regional Government is the regional head as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs which are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Regional Head hereinafter referred to as Regent is the Regent of Balangan Regency.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the regional people's representative institution of Balangan Regency which is positioned as an element of the Regional Government administration.
5. Agency or Board is an Agency or Board whose scope of duties and responsibilities includes the field of protection and empowerment of women and children in the region. 6. Woman is an adult human being of female sex and a person who is recognized by law as a woman. 7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years including a child who is still in the womb. 8. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
9. Family is a person who has a blood relationship in a straight line upward or downward and in a collateral line up to the third degree, or who has a marital relationship, or a person who is a dependent of a woman and/or child.
10. Parent is biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 11. Protection of women and children is an effort to prevent and handle all forms of acts of violence including neglect and trafficking in persons that violate the human rights of women and children, as well as to provide basic and specific services for the needs of women and children in the conditions and situations they experience. 12. Prevention is an activity carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children.
13. Service is an activity and immediate action carried out by Professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
14. Empowerment of women and children is an effort to strengthen human rights, improve quality of life and increase the participation of women and children in their social interaction.
15. Victim of acts of violence is an individual or group of people who experience suffering whether physical, mental or emotional, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights (HAM) violations, or criminal acts as well as acts of violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or regional government apparatus or by individuals.
16. Assistance is an activity and action carried out by an assistant during the service process.
17. Assistant is a person or representative of an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance.
18. Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims from psychosocial disorders and the restoration of normal social functioning, both in the family and in the community.
19. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, community, institutions, or other social environments that can provide protection.
20. Safe House is a temporary residence, provided to give protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards. 21. Regional Action Plan is a foundation and guideline for related agencies, vertical agencies, and the community, in order to carry out activities for the implementation of prevention and protection of women and children victims of acts of violence.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Violence against women and children is one form of act that violates human rights, because the right to protection from violence of a woman that has been guaranteed by the 1945 Constitution and the Law on Human Rights has been violated by the perpetrator of violence, which should be respected and enforced to enhance human dignity, welfare and justice for such women. The impact of such violence causes women or children to suffer physically, psychologically, mentally, sexually, so they need to receive protection and health rehabilitation services, social rehabilitation, repatriation and legal assistance carried out in an integrated manner by victim service providers established by the Government, Regional Government and the community.

The protection and empowerment of women and children is currently a focus in development. Women and children are usually made into one unit in the scope of their regulation so that it is not focused and results in ambiguity between women and children. Women can be adults or children, while children can be female or male. In the division of authority as determined in Law Number 23 Year 2014 concerning Regional Government, it has been focused on the scope of each form of handling, namely women and children are not a unity. In that context, regionally related to women and children, regional regulations must be present concerning: a). Fulfillment of Children's Rights and Special Protection of Children, b). Gender Mainstreaming, c). Protection of Witnesses/Victims and Prevention of Trafficking in Persons, and d). Protection and Empowerment of Women and Children From Acts of Violence. These four regional regulations are a package that must be regulated by the Regional Government in accordance with its authority.

CHAPTER X REGIONAL ACTION PLAN

Article 20 (1) The Regent may establish a regional action plan related to the protection and empowerment of women and children.

2. The regional action plan as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be realized in a joint commitment of all elements in the region to implement the protection and empowerment of women and children and eliminate all forms of violence, neglect and trafficking in persons.

OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE.

CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1 In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is the Region of Balangan Regency.
2. Regional Government is the regional head as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs which are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Regional Head hereinafter referred to as Regent is the Regent of Balangan Regency.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the regional people's representative institution of Balangan Regency which is positioned as an element of the Regional Government administration.
5. Agency or Board is an Agency or Board whose scope of duties and responsibilities includes the field of protection and empowerment of women and children in the region. 6. Woman is an adult human being of female sex and a person who is recognized by law as a woman. 7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years including a child who is still in the womb. 8. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
9. Family is a person who has a blood relationship in a straight line upward or downward and in a collateral line up to the third degree, or who has a marital relationship, or a person who is a dependent of a woman and/or child.
10. Parent is biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 11. Protection of women and children is an effort to prevent and handle all forms of acts of violence including neglect and trafficking in persons that violate the human rights of women and children, as well as to provide basic and specific services for the needs of women and children in the conditions and situations they experience. 12. Prevention is an activity carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children.
13. Service is an activity and immediate action carried out by Professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
14. Empowerment of women and children is an effort to strengthen human rights, improve quality of life and increase the participation of women and children in their social interaction.
15. Victim of acts of violence is an individual or group of people who experience suffering whether physical, mental or emotional, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights (HAM) violations, or criminal acts as well as acts of violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or regional government apparatus or by individuals.
16. Assistance is an activity and action carried out by an assistant during the service process.
17. Assistant is a person or representative of an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance.
18. Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims from psychosocial disorders and the restoration of normal social functioning, both in the family and in the community.
19. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, community, institutions, or other social environments that can provide protection.
20. Safe House is a temporary residence, provided to give protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards. 21. Regional Action Plan is a foundation and guideline for related agencies, vertical agencies, and the community, in order to carry out activities for the implementation of prevention and protection of women and children victims of acts of violence.

ACTING REGENT OF BALANGAN,

H. M. HAWARI

ON

REGIONAL REGULATION OF BALANGAN REGENCY NUMBER 3 YEAR 2016

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Violence against women and children is one form of act that violates human rights, because the right to protection from violence of a woman that has been guaranteed by the 1945 Constitution and the Law on Human Rights has been violated by the perpetrator of violence, which should be respected and enforced to enhance human dignity, welfare and justice for such women. The impact of such violence causes women or children to suffer physically, psychologically, mentally, sexually, so they need to receive protection and health rehabilitation services, social rehabilitation, repatriation and legal assistance carried out in an integrated manner by victim service providers established by the Government, Regional Government and the community.

The protection and empowerment of women and children is currently a focus in development. Women and children are usually made into one unit in the scope of their regulation so that it is not focused and results in ambiguity between women and children. Women can be adults or children, while children can be female or male. In the division of authority as determined in Law Number 23 Year 2014 concerning Regional Government, it has been focused on the scope of each form of handling, namely women and children are not a unity. In that context, regionally related to women and children, regional regulations must be present concerning: a). Fulfillment of Children's Rights and Special Protection of Children, b). Gender Mainstreaming, c). Protection of Witnesses/Victims and Prevention of Trafficking in Persons, and d). Protection and Empowerment of Women and Children From Acts of Violence. These four regional regulations are a package that must be regulated by the Regional Government in accordance with its authority.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 1Sufficiently clear

Article 2Paragraph (1) Sufficiently clear Paragraph (2) What is meant by "the best interests of women and children" is all best actions concerning victims carried out by the Government, society, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, therefore the best interests of victims must be the primary consideration. Article 3Paragraph (1) Sufficiently clear Paragraph (2) Point a What is meant by "physical violence" is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causing death. Point b What is meant by "sexual violence" is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain purposes. Point c What is meant by "psychological violence" is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering to a person. Point d What is meant by intimidation is an act of ordering or prohibiting by means of threatening or restraining to cause harm so that the victim is unable to make choices for their best interests. Point e What is meant by forced eviction is an act of ordering by force or with physical force not to be in a safe place or position as is the right possessed by a person to a place suitable for them. Point f What is meant by deprivation of liberty is an act of eliminating the right to live based on the best interests of a person. Point g What is meant by neglect is:
a. actions that result in the failure to fulfill a child's needs properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social; b. actions of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or take care of a child as appropriate; c. actions that neglect a person within their household scope, whereas according to the law applicable to them or because of an agreement or contract they are obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to that person; d. actions that result in economic dependence by limiting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person. Point h What is meant by "exploitation" includes:
a. actions that exploit a child economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others; b. actions with or without the victim's consent which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial. c. all forms of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of victims to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or indecency. What is meant by "trafficking in persons" is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited. In such conditions there is a need for a mediator, preventer or separator and separation of the parties so that unwanted things do not occur. Paragraph (2) Sufficiently clear Paragraph (3) What is meant by taking into account the condition, problem situation and form of handling is not ambiguous or haphazard so as to create a condition that is the reverse of the desire to improve the situation becoming deeper in conflict and can bring negative value in the future. Paragraph (4) Sufficiently clear Article 5Paragraph (1) Sufficiently clear Paragraph (2) Sufficiently clear Article 6Paragraph (1) Sufficiently clear Paragraph (2) Point a What is meant by complaint is a statement from a witness or victim that must be responded to by the authorized Official. Point b What is meant by health rehabilitation is the provision of medical services/health treatment in the form of care and recovery of injuries or physical condition of victims and reproductive health by medical personnel and paramedics including medicolegal services for proof in the legal field. Point c What is meant by social rehabilitation is the restoration of social and economic rights for women or children who experience acts of violence or neglect. Point d What is meant by social reintegration is an effort to guarantee rights related to status as a family member or community member and the provision of economic independence services in the form of skills training and providing economic access so that victims can be independent. Point e What is meant by legal assistance and accompaniment is: a. confidential handling or placement of victims in safe locations and houses whose whereabouts are kept secret to avoid intimidation and threats; b. protection by law enforcement officers; c. provision of information regarding legal rights and obligations to victims or guardians of victims and identification of incidents; d. accompaniment for legal processes and obtaining compensation or compensation rights; and e. facilitating and mediating household disputes to realize harmonious and prosperous household integrity.

CHAPTER II PRINCIPLES AND OBJECTIVES

Article 2 (1) Protection of women and children from acts of violence is conducted based on the principles of: a. respect for human rights; b. non-discrimination; and c. protection of victims.

2. Protection of women and children from acts of violence aims to protect, respect, guarantee the human rights of women and children, and pursue the best interests of women and children.

CHAPTER X REGIONAL ACTION PLAN

Article 20 (1) The Regent may establish a regional action plan related to the protection and empowerment of women and children.

2. The regional action plan as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be realized in a joint commitment of all elements in the region to implement the protection and empowerment of women and children and eliminate all forms of violence, neglect and trafficking in persons.

CHAPTER V SERVICES

Article 6 (1) The Regional Government provides services to women and children victims of acts of violence and neglect.

2. Services as referred to in paragraph (1) are in the form of: a. complaints; b. health rehabilitation;
c. social rehabilitation;

d. social reintegration; and e. legal assistance and accompaniment.

Article 7 (1) Women and children victims of acts of violence are placed in safe houses or places whose whereabouts are kept confidential and receive basic fulfillment in accordance with their rights.

2. Child victims of acts of violence who are placed in safe houses are provided with care in accordance with their needs.

CHAPTER XI FUNDING

Article 21 (1) Funding for the Protection and Empowerment of Women and Children shall be charged to the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget.

Promulgated in Paringin on January 20, 2016 (2) In addition to funds from the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget, funding may come from non-binding assistance or contributions from third parties.

3. Technically and for the operation of the Center for Protection and Empowerment of Women and Children, it shall be placed in the budget item of the Agency determined by the Regent.
4. The allocation of funds by the Center for Protection and Empowerment of Women and Children shall be based on the established work program.
5. Accountability for the use of funds for the implementation of protection of women and children shall be in accordance with the provisions of applicable laws and regulations.

CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1 In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is the Region of Balangan Regency.
2. Regional Government is the regional head as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs which are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Regional Head hereinafter referred to as Regent is the Regent of Balangan Regency.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the regional people's representative institution of Balangan Regency which is positioned as an element of the Regional Government administration.
5. Agency or Board is an Agency or Board whose scope of duties and responsibilities includes the field of protection and empowerment of women and children in the region. 6. Woman is an adult human being of female sex and a person who is recognized by law as a woman. 7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years including a child who is still in the womb. 8. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
9. Family is a person who has a blood relationship in a straight line upward or downward and in a collateral line up to the third degree, or who has a marital relationship, or a person who is a dependent of a woman and/or child.
10. Parent is biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 11. Protection of women and children is an effort to prevent and handle all forms of acts of violence including neglect and trafficking in persons that violate the human rights of women and children, as well as to provide basic and specific services for the needs of women and children in the conditions and situations they experience. 12. Prevention is an activity carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children.
13. Service is an activity and immediate action carried out by Professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
14. Empowerment of women and children is an effort to strengthen human rights, improve quality of life and increase the participation of women and children in their social interaction.
15. Victim of acts of violence is an individual or group of people who experience suffering whether physical, mental or emotional, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights (HAM) violations, or criminal acts as well as acts of violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or regional government apparatus or by individuals.
16. Assistance is an activity and action carried out by an assistant during the service process.
17. Assistant is a person or representative of an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance.
18. Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims from psychosocial disorders and the restoration of normal social functioning, both in the family and in the community.
19. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, community, institutions, or other social environments that can provide protection.
20. Safe House is a temporary residence, provided to give protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards. 21. Regional Action Plan is a foundation and guideline for related agencies, vertical agencies, and the community, in order to carry out activities for the implementation of prevention and protection of women and children victims of acts of violence.

Article 21 (1) Funding for the Protection and Empowerment of Women and Children shall be charged to the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget.

Promulgated in Paringin on January 20, 2016 (2) In addition to funds from the Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget, funding may come from non-binding assistance or contributions from third parties.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Violence against women and children is one form of act that violates human rights, because the right to protection from violence of a woman that has been guaranteed by the 1945 Constitution and the Law on Human Rights has been violated by the perpetrator of violence, which should be respected and enforced to enhance human dignity, welfare and justice for such women. The impact of such violence causes women or children to suffer physically, psychologically, mentally, sexually, so they need to receive protection and health rehabilitation services, social rehabilitation, repatriation and legal assistance carried out in an integrated manner by victim service providers established by the Government, Regional Government and the community.

The protection and empowerment of women and children is currently a focus in development. Women and children are usually made into one unit in the scope of their regulation so that it is not focused and results in ambiguity between women and children. Women can be adults or children, while children can be female or male. In the division of authority as determined in Law Number 23 Year 2014 concerning Regional Government, it has been focused on the scope of each form of handling, namely women and children are not a unity. In that context, regionally related to women and children, regional regulations must be present concerning: a). Fulfillment of Children's Rights and Special Protection of Children, b). Gender Mainstreaming, c). Protection of Witnesses/Victims and Prevention of Trafficking in Persons, and d). Protection and Empowerment of Women and Children From Acts of Violence. These four regional regulations are a package that must be regulated by the Regional Government in accordance with its authority.

5. Agency or Board is an Agency or Board whose scope of duties and responsibilities includes the field of protection and empowerment of women and children in the region. 6. Woman is an adult human being of female sex and a person who is recognized by law as a woman. 7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years including a child who is still in the womb. 8. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
9. Family is a person who has a blood relationship in a straight line upward or downward and in a collateral line up to the third degree, or who has a marital relationship, or a person who is a dependent of a woman and/or child.
10. Parent is biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 11. Protection of women and children is an effort to prevent and handle all forms of acts of violence including neglect and trafficking in persons that violate the human rights of women and children, as well as to provide basic and specific services for the needs of women and children in the conditions and situations they experience. 12. Prevention is an activity carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children.
13. Service is an activity and immediate action carried out by Professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
14. Empowerment of women and children is an effort to strengthen human rights, improve quality of life and increase the participation of women and children in their social interaction.
15. Victim of acts of violence is an individual or group of people who experience suffering whether physical, mental or emotional, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights (HAM) violations, or criminal acts as well as acts of violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or regional government apparatus or by individuals.
16. Assistance is an activity and action carried out by an assistant during the service process.
17. Assistant is a person or representative of an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance.
18. Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims from psychosocial disorders and the restoration of normal social functioning, both in the family and in the community.
19. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, community, institutions, or other social environments that can provide protection.
20. Safe House is a temporary residence, provided to give protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards. 21. Regional Action Plan is a foundation and guideline for related agencies, vertical agencies, and the community, in order to carry out activities for the implementation of prevention and protection of women and children victims of acts of violence.

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Violence against women and children is one form of act that violates human rights, because the right to protection from violence of a woman that has been guaranteed by the 1945 Constitution and the Law on Human Rights has been violated by the perpetrator of violence, which should be respected and enforced to enhance human dignity, welfare and justice for such women. The impact of such violence causes women or children to suffer physically, psychologically, mentally, sexually, so they need to receive protection and health rehabilitation services, social rehabilitation, repatriation and legal assistance carried out in an integrated manner by victim service providers established by the Government, Regional Government and the community.

The protection and empowerment of women and children is currently a focus in development. Women and children are usually made into one unit in the scope of their regulation so that it is not focused and results in ambiguity between women and children. Women can be adults or children, while children can be female or male. In the division of authority as determined in Law Number 23 Year 2014 concerning Regional Government, it has been focused on the scope of each form of handling, namely women and children are not a unity. In that context, regionally related to women and children, regional regulations must be present concerning: a). Fulfillment of Children's Rights and Special Protection of Children, b). Gender Mainstreaming, c). Protection of Witnesses/Victims and Prevention of Trafficking in Persons, and d). Protection and Empowerment of Women and Children From Acts of Violence. These four regional regulations are a package that must be regulated by the Regional Government in accordance with its authority.

4. The allocation of funds by the Center for Protection and Empowerment of Women and Children shall be based on the established work program.
5. Accountability for the use of funds for the implementation of protection of women and children shall be in accordance with the provisions of applicable laws and regulations.

CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1 In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Region is the Region of Balangan Regency.
2. Regional Government is the regional head as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs which are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Regional Head hereinafter referred to as Regent is the Regent of Balangan Regency.
4. Regional House of Representatives hereinafter abbreviated as DPRD is the regional people's representative institution of Balangan Regency which is positioned as an element of the Regional Government administration.
5. Agency or Board is an Agency or Board whose scope of duties and responsibilities includes the field of protection and empowerment of women and children in the region. 6. Woman is an adult human being of female sex and a person who is recognized by law as a woman. 7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years including a child who is still in the womb. 8. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
9. Family is a person who has a blood relationship in a straight line upward or downward and in a collateral line up to the third degree, or who has a marital relationship, or a person who is a dependent of a woman and/or child.
10. Parent is biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 11. Protection of women and children is an effort to prevent and handle all forms of acts of violence including neglect and trafficking in persons that violate the human rights of women and children, as well as to provide basic and specific services for the needs of women and children in the conditions and situations they experience. 12. Prevention is an activity carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children.
13. Service is an activity and immediate action carried out by Professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
14. Empowerment of women and children is an effort to strengthen human rights, improve quality of life and increase the participation of women and children in their social interaction.
15. Victim of acts of violence is an individual or group of people who experience suffering whether physical, mental or emotional, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights (HAM) violations, or criminal acts as well as acts of violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or regional government apparatus or by individuals.
16. Assistance is an activity and action carried out by an assistant during the service process.
17. Assistant is a person or representative of an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance.
18. Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims from psychosocial disorders and the restoration of normal social functioning, both in the family and in the community.
19. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, community, institutions, or other social environments that can provide protection.
20. Safe House is a temporary residence, provided to give protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards. 21. Regional Action Plan is a foundation and guideline for related agencies, vertical agencies, and the community, in order to carry out activities for the implementation of prevention and protection of women and children victims of acts of violence.

ON

REGIONAL REGULATION OF BALANGAN REGENCY NUMBER 3 YEAR 2016

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Violence against women and children is one form of act that violates human rights, because the right to protection from violence of a woman that has been guaranteed by the 1945 Constitution and the Law on Human Rights has been violated by the perpetrator of violence, which should be respected and enforced to enhance human dignity, welfare and justice for such women. The impact of such violence causes women or children to suffer physically, psychologically, mentally, sexually, so they need to receive protection and health rehabilitation services, social rehabilitation, repatriation and legal assistance carried out in an integrated manner by victim service providers established by the Government, Regional Government and the community.

The protection and empowerment of women and children is currently a focus in development. Women and children are usually made into one unit in the scope of their regulation so that it is not focused and results in ambiguity between women and children. Women can be adults or children, while children can be female or male. In the division of authority as determined in Law Number 23 Year 2014 concerning Regional Government, it has been focused on the scope of each form of handling, namely women and children are not a unity. In that context, regionally related to women and children, regional regulations must be present concerning: a). Fulfillment of Children's Rights and Special Protection of Children, b). Gender Mainstreaming, c). Protection of Witnesses/Victims and Prevention of Trafficking in Persons, and d). Protection and Empowerment of Women and Children From Acts of Violence. These four regional regulations are a package that must be regulated by the Regional Government in accordance with its authority.

CHAPTER I GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1 In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

5. Agency or Board is an Agency or Board whose scope of duties and responsibilities includes the field of protection and empowerment of women and children in the region. 6. Woman is an adult human being of female sex and a person who is recognized by law as a woman. 7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years including a child who is still in the womb. 8. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and/or community organizations.
9. Family is a person who has a blood relationship in a straight line upward or downward and in a collateral line up to the third degree, or who has a marital relationship, or a person who is a dependent of a woman and/or child.
10. Parent is biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother. 11. Protection of women and children is an effort to prevent and handle all forms of acts of violence including neglect and trafficking in persons that violate the human rights of women and children, as well as to provide basic and specific services for the needs of women and children in the conditions and situations they experience. 12. Prevention is an activity carried out to prevent the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children.
13. Service is an activity and immediate action carried out by Professional personnel in accordance with their respective professions in the form of counseling, therapy and advocacy for the strengthening and recovery of victims of violence.
14. Empowerment of women and children is an effort to strengthen human rights, improve quality of life and increase the participation of women and children in their social interaction.
15. Victim of acts of violence is an individual or group of people who experience suffering whether physical, mental or emotional, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights (HAM) violations, or criminal acts as well as acts of violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or regional government apparatus or by individuals.
16. Assistance is an activity and action carried out by an assistant during the service process.
17. Assistant is a person or representative of an institution who has the expertise to provide assistance.
18. Rehabilitation is the recovery of victims from psychosocial disorders and the restoration of normal social functioning, both in the family and in the community.
19. Social Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, community, institutions, or other social environments that can provide protection.
20. Safe House is a temporary residence, provided to give protection to victims in accordance with predetermined standards. 21. Regional Action Plan is a foundation and guideline for related agencies, vertical agencies, and the community, in order to carry out activities for the implementation of prevention and protection of women and children victims of acts of violence.

REGIONAL REGULATION OF BALANGAN REGENCY NUMBER 3 YEAR 2016

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Violence against women and children is one form of act that violates human rights, because the right to protection from violence of a woman that has been guaranteed by the 1945 Constitution and the Law on Human Rights has been violated by the perpetrator of violence, which should be respected and enforced to enhance human dignity, welfare and justice for such women. The impact of such violence causes women or children to suffer physically, psychologically, mentally, sexually, so they need to receive protection and health rehabilitation services, social rehabilitation, repatriation and legal assistance carried out in an integrated manner by victim service providers established by the Government, Regional Government and the community.

The protection and empowerment of women and children is currently a focus in development. Women and children are usually made into one unit in the scope of their regulation so that it is not focused and results in ambiguity between women and children. Women can be adults or children, while children can be female or male. In the division of authority as determined in Law Number 23 Year 2014 concerning Regional Government, it has been focused on the scope of each form of handling, namely women and children are not a unity. In that context, regionally related to women and children, regional regulations must be present concerning: a). Fulfillment of Children's Rights and Special Protection of Children, b). Gender Mainstreaming, c). Protection of Witnesses/Victims and Prevention of Trafficking in Persons, and d). Protection and Empowerment of Women and Children From Acts of Violence. These four regional regulations are a package that must be regulated by the Regional Government in accordance with its authority.

Article 20 (1) The Regent may establish a regional action plan related to the protection and empowerment of women and children.

2. The regional action plan as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be realized in a joint commitment of all elements in the region to implement the protection and empowerment of women and children and eliminate all forms of violence, neglect and trafficking in persons.

ACTING REGENT OF BALANGAN,

H. M. HAWARI

ELUCIDATION

ON

REGIONAL REGULATION OF BALANGAN REGENCY NUMBER 3 YEAR 2016

CONCERNING

PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE

I. GENERAL

Violence against women and children is one form of act that violates human rights, because the right to protection from violence of a woman that has been guaranteed by the 1945 Constitution and the Law on Human Rights has been violated by the perpetrator of violence, which should be respected and enforced to enhance human dignity, welfare and justice for such women. The impact of such violence causes women or children to suffer physically, psychologically, mentally, sexually, so they need to receive protection and health rehabilitation services, social rehabilitation, repatriation and legal assistance carried out in an integrated manner by victim service providers established by the Government, Regional Government and the community.

The protection and empowerment of women and children is currently a focus in development. Women and children are usually made into one unit in the scope of their regulation so that it is not focused and results in ambiguity between women and children. Women can be adults or children, while children can be female or male. In the division of authority as determined in Law Number 23 Year 2014 concerning Regional Government, it has been focused on the scope of each form of handling, namely women and children are not a unity. In that context, regionally related to women and children, regional regulations must be present concerning: a). Fulfillment of Children's Rights and Special Protection of Children, b). Gender Mainstreaming, c). Protection of Witnesses/Victims and Prevention of Trafficking in Persons, and d). Protection and Empowerment of Women and Children From Acts of Violence. These four regional regulations are a package that must be regulated by the Regional Government in accordance with its authority.

Article 1Sufficiently clear

Article 2Paragraph (1) Sufficiently clear Paragraph (2) What is meant by "the best interests of women and children" is all best actions concerning victims carried out by the Government, society, legislative bodies and judicial bodies, therefore the best interests of victims must be the primary consideration. Article 3Paragraph (1) Sufficiently clear Paragraph (2) Point a What is meant by "physical violence" is any act that results in pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causing death. Point b What is meant by "sexual violence" is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse, forced unnatural or unwanted sexual intercourse, forced sexual intercourse with others for commercial purposes and or certain purposes. Point c What is meant by "psychological violence" is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering to a person. Point d What is meant by intimidation is an act of ordering or prohibiting by means of threatening or restraining to cause harm so that the victim is unable to make choices for their best interests. Point e What is meant by forced eviction is an act of ordering by force or with physical force not to be in a safe place or position as is the right possessed by a person to a place suitable for them. Point f What is meant by deprivation of liberty is an act of eliminating the right to live based on the best interests of a person. Point g What is meant by neglect is:
a. actions that result in the failure to fulfill a child's needs properly, whether physical, mental, spiritual or social; b. actions of deliberately neglecting to maintain, care for, or take care of a child as appropriate; c. actions that neglect a person within their household scope, whereas according to the law applicable to them or because of an agreement or contract they are obliged to provide livelihood, care, or maintenance to that person; d. actions that result in economic dependence by limiting and/or prohibiting proper work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person. Point h What is meant by "exploitation" includes:
a. actions that exploit a child economically or sexually with the intention of benefiting oneself or others; b. actions with or without the victim's consent which include but are not limited to prostitution, forced labor or services, slavery or similar practices, oppression, extortion, utilization of physical, sexual, reproductive organs, or unlawfully removing or transplanting organs and/or body tissues or utilizing the labor or ability of a person by another party to obtain benefits both material and immaterial. c. all forms of utilization of sexual organs or other body organs of victims to obtain benefits, including but not limited to all activities of prostitution or indecency. What is meant by "trafficking in persons" is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or vulnerable position, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited. Point b What is meant by health rehabilitation is the provision of medical services/health treatment in the form of care and recovery of injuries or physical condition of victims and reproductive health by medical personnel and paramedics including medicolegal services for proof in the legal field. Point c What is meant by social rehabilitation is the restoration of social and economic rights for women or children who experience acts of violence or neglect. CHAPTER II PRINCIPLES AND OBJECTIVES

Article 2 (1) Protection of women and children from acts of violence is conducted based on the principles of: a. respect for human rights; b. non-discrimination; and c. protection of victims.

2. Protection of women and children from acts of violence aims to protect, respect, guarantee the human rights of women and children, and pursue the best interests of women and children.

CHAPTER XIII CLOSING PROVISIONS
